title: Reliability Onboarding and Collaboration Blueprint - Q3 2026
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working blueprint for bringing product teams and platform teams together to adopt Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and operational practices. It focuses on a light-weight, repeatable onboarding sequence and a collaboration cadence that minimizes friction for teams shipping new services or migrating existing ones to SRE stewardship.

Scope:
- Services: internal and customer-facing API endpoints, streaming routes, batch inference pipelines, and the control plane features managed by Platform.
- Activities: SLO definition, baseline measurement, alert configuration, runbook creation, and a first 90-day reliability plan.
- Not covered: hiring, budget approvals, or deep architectural rewrites (those are escalations).

Goals (90-day):
- Every onboarded service has at least one availability SLO and one latency SLO defined and recorded in the SLO registry.
- Onboarded services have basic alerting tied to error budget burn and a one-author runbook stub.
- Reduce time-to-onboard from kickoff to first SLO measurement to <= 4 weeks for simple services.

Success metrics (tracked weekly):
- % of target services with SLOs in registry (target 80% by end of Q3).
- Median days from kickoff to first SLO baseline measurement (target <= 28).
- Number of alert noise incidents attributable to misconfigured SLO alerts (target zero after 2-week post-onboard review).

High-level onboarding flow (phases):
1) Kickoff (0): 30–60 min sync. Who: Service Owner, SRE liaison, Infra lead. Output: onboarding ticket, initial risk assessment, list of key paths (happy + error).
2) Measurement & baseline (week 1–2): Instrument metrics, validate telemetry (latency, success rate, traffic split). Output: baseline charts, suggested SLO thresholds.
3) SLO definition & agreement (week 2): Create SLOs (objective, window, indicators), agree on error budget policy and oncall responsibilities.
4) Alert & runbook (week 3): Deploy alert rules that respect burn pacing, create a minimum runbook with postmortem link template.
5) Review & harden (week 4–8): Watch error budget for two weeks, adjust thresholds or mitigations, finalize docs.

Roles and responsibilities (handshake model):
- SRE liaison: shepherd the onboarding, provide SLO template, run a 2-week quiet-window review, escalate platform gaps.
- Service Owner (product/engineer): responsible for defining critical user journeys, approving SLA-like commitments, and owning fixes.
- Infra/Platform Engineer: ensure telemetry collection, assist with alerting plumbing, and provide deployment knobs (rate-limiting, circuit-breakers).
- Observability Owner: help produce dashboards and SLO registry entries.

Cadence and rituals:
- Weekly 30-min onboarding standup during active onboardings (Tue 10am). Purpose: unblock, review next steps, quick decisions.
- SLO Sync (biweekly, 60 min): cross-functional forum for SLO policy changes, template updates, and notable learnings from recent onboardings.
- Monthly reliability review: exec-facing summary of adoption, top incidents, and improvements.

Onboarding checklist (service owner copy):
- [ ] Create onboarding ticket and attach initial telemetry links.
- [ ] Identify two critical user journeys and map SLI events.
- [ ] Ensure metrics emitted include request_id / trace_id for correlation.
- [ ] Add SLOs to registry draft and propose error budget policy.
- [ ] Implement alerting rules and verify alert routing to oncall.
- [ ] Add runbook with triage steps and postmortem template.
- [ ] Schedule 2-week post-onboard noise review with SRE liaison.

SLO template (short):
- Service name: 
- SLO name: availability / latency / freshness
- Indicator (SLI): e.g., p95 latency < 300ms on production reads
- Objective: 99.9% over 30d (or tailored)
- Window: rolling 30d
- Error budget policy: burn rate thresholds and automated mitigations (if any)
- Owner: name + team
- Dashboard link: 
- Alert links:

Cross-team handoffs and dependencies:
- Telemetry gaps: Infra must commit to emitting stable metric names. If missing, escalate via SRE-ops channel within 48h.
- Library support: DevX may need a small client lib change; prioritize as low-latency PR with a 5-day SLAT for release.
- Capacity/Scaling: If SLO requires dedicated capacity changes (e.g., reserved GPUs), trigger Dedicated capacity request and include timeline in onboarding ticket.

Operational examples (templates):
- Canary rollout with SLO guard: before a rollout, run a 24h canary window where SLO burn is measured. If burn rate exceeds 3x expected, auto-rollback rule executed (if supported) or paging to oncall.
- Feature flag gating: use boolean flags to limit exposure and tie flag percentage to observed error budget consumption.

Risk register & mitigations:
- Risk: Teams under-define indicators and choose easy SLOs -> Mitigation: Mandatory 1:1 review of SLI mapping by SRE liaison.
- Risk: Alert fatigue caused by sensitivity mismatch -> Mitigation: Two-week quiet-window test and a noise review with remediation tasks.
- Risk: Missing telemetry for batch jobs -> Mitigation: Provide a lightweight batch telemetry checklist and a follow-up ticket to infra.

Communication channels and artifacts:
- Slack: #sre-onboarding (primary), #sre-escalations (for urgent incidents).
- Confluence: canonical SLO registry and templates (linked above).
- Jira workflow: use the SRE-Onboard project for tracking (JIRA-SRE-4321 as example).

Next steps (near-term action items):
- Aisha: finalize this blueprint and post to Confluence (due 2026-08-06).
- Miguel: prepare the onboarding Checklist template and create a starter dashboard (due 2026-08-09).
- Priya: prototype a simple client library PR to emit standard SLI labels (target 2026-08-16).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Error budget automation: do we enable auto-throttles for non-critical routes or keep manual? Tradeoffs doc needed.
- Compliance: how should SLO reporting be surfaced for Private deployments where telemetry may be restricted? Need legal/infra input.

Notes to self (working):
- Keep templates pragmatic — start small and iterate based on noise and adoption.
- Low-friction wins: dashboards + runbooks are more impactful early than perfect SLO thresholds.

Appendix: quick links and references:
- SLO registries and previous onboarding retros: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Onboard+Retros
- Example onboarding ticket template: JIRA-SRE-4321

End of blueprint.

(Informal draft — expect edits and additions from collaborators above; treat the timeline as optimistic for simple services.)
